sections.overview: This small caponiid spider is known from California’s Coast Ranges and is the sole described species of the genus Calponia.
sections.identification: Unlike most North American caponiids, which have only two eyes, it retains eight eyes arranged in two rows, an unusual ancestral-looking trait within the family.
sections.habitat: It has been found in oak woodland beneath rocks, leaf litter and other ground debris in the California Coast Ranges.
sections.diet: Direct observations of this species’ feeding are scarce; family-level accounts describe caponiids as wandering hunters that prey on other spiders.
sections.behavior: It is a ground-dwelling spider that shelters under cover, but its natural history remains poorly documented compared with familiar web-building spiders.
sections.reproduction: The consulted species descriptions do not establish detailed courtship, egg-sac or juvenile-development schedules for this spider.
sections.ecology: The related North American caponiid Orthonops gertschi has only two eyes, making eye number a striking contrast between these family relatives.
sections.conservation: Its known range is geographically restricted, but the consulted taxonomic and natural-history sources provide no formal global threat category.
